question: What is the primary function of the urinary bladder in the human body?
explanation: The bladder acts primarily as a holding reservoir to collect urine until it can be conveniently eliminated from the body. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T3#GNS121_U2_T3_h1)

question: Why does the trigone, the smooth triangular area on the floor of the bladder, stay smooth when the bladder fills?

options.A: It lacks any sensory nerve endings to detect stretch
options.B: It receives a continuous direct blood supply
options.C: Its lining is firmly attached to the muscle underneath
options.D: It is constantly bathed by concentrated fluid

explanation: Unlike the rest of the bladder wall which folds into rugae, the trigone mucosa stays flat because it is tightly anchored to the underlying muscle. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T3#GNS121_U2_T3_h1)

question: Which type of tissue lines the inside of the urinary bladder so it can stretch?
explanation: Transitional epithelium stretches easily to accommodate varying volumes of fluid as the bladder fills and empties. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T3#GNS121_U2_T3_h2)

question: What is the main job of the detrusor muscle in the bladder wall?

options.A: Sensing the chemical composition of urine
options.C: Producing mucus to protect the lining

explanation: The intertwined smooth muscle layers of the detrusor muscle contract powerfully to empty the bladder during urination. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T3#GNS121_U2_T3_h2)

question: Arterial blood flows to the urinary bladder mainly through branches of which major artery?
explanation: The internal iliac arteries provide the primary branches, including the vesical arteries, that feed the bladder tissues. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T3#GNS121_U2_T3_h3)

question: Where does blood from the urinary bladder drain into on its way back to the heart?
explanation: The vesical venous plexus empties directly into the internal iliac veins to return deoxygenated blood to systemic circulation. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T3#GNS121_U2_T3_h3)

question: Which nerve carries signals to control the voluntary external urethral sphincter?
explanation: The pudendal nerve provides voluntary control over the skeletal muscle of the external urethral sphincter. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T3#GNS121_U2_T3_h4)

question: How does the sympathetic nervous system affect the urinary bladder?

options.A: Promotes urine storage by relaxing the detrusor
options.B: Relaxes the external sphincter for elimination
options.C: Triggers powerful contractions to empty the organ

explanation: Sympathetic pathways suppress bladder contraction and close the internal sphincter to keep urine inside the reservoir. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T3#GNS121_U2_T3_h4)

question: At approximately what volume do stretch receptors in the adult bladder typically trigger initial awareness of fullness?
explanation: Normal sensory awareness and desire to void usually begin when bladder volume reaches this range. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T3#GNS121_U2_T3_h5)

question: What happens in the lower urinary tract right before urine is passed out of the body?

options.B: The detrusor muscle remains completely relaxed

explanation: Voluntary relaxation of the skeletal muscle in the external sphincter allows urine to pass out through the urethra once the detrusor contracts. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T3#GNS121_U2_T3_h5)

question: What is the medical term for painful or difficult urination often seen in bladder infections?
explanation: Dysuria describes the burning or discomfort experienced during urine elimination, typical of cystitis. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T3#GNS121_U2_T3_h6)

question: Which tool helps a nurse safely measure how much urine is left in the bladder right after a patient urinates?
explanation: A portable ultrasound device provides a quick, non-invasive method to estimate the volume of urine remaining in the bladder after voiding. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T3#GNS121_U2_T3_h6)
